He finished the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 NCAA Division I season]] as the top scorer in the nation at 25.0 [[point (basketball)|points]] per game while scoring a total of 801 points.{{cite web| title =Points Per Game Leaders| work =2012–13 Men's Basketball Statistics| publisher =[[National Collegiate Athletic Association]]| date =February 24, 2013| url =http://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/136| accessdate = February 26, 2013}} He is also considered a potential draft selection in June's [[2013 NBA Draft]].{{cite web| title =Erick Green| work =Mock 2013 NBA Draft| publisher =DraftExpress.com| date =February 26, 2013| url =http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Erick-Green-16580/stats/| accessdate = February 27, 2013}} ==High school== Green was born in [[Inglewood, California]] but grew up in [[Winchester, Virginia]].{{cite web| title =#1 Erick Green| work =HokiesSports.com| publisher =Virginia Tech| year=2013| url =http://www.hokiesports.com/mbasketball/players/green_erick.html| accessdate = February 27, 2013}} He spent the first three years of his prep career at his hometown's [[Millbrook High School]], then transferred for his senior year to [[Fairfax, Virginia|Fairfax]]'s [[Paul VI Catholic High School]]. Between the two schools, Green earned four varsity letters. In his lone year at Paul VI he led the Panthers to a state championship (coincidentally, Green had led Millbrook to a state championship the previous season) and was named the 2009 Division I Independent League Player of the Year. After Paul VI's championship he was named an EA Sports All-American. ''[[The Washington Post]]'' also selected him to their All-Metro Team, the [[Associated Press]] picked him as their Virginia Group AA Player of the Year, and Green was named the district and region player of the year. ==College career== Green struggled his [[freshman]] season in [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]] and averaged just 2.6 points per game and shot 29.3% from the field.{{cite web| title =Erick Green stats| work =sports-reference.com| publisher =Sports Reference LLC| year=2013| url =http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/erick-green-1.html| accessdate = March 1, 2013}}{{cite web| last =Giannotto| first =Mark| title =For Virginia Tech’s Erick Green, success at the rim started in the gym| publisher =''[[The Washington Post]]''| date =February 20, 2013| url =http://articles.washingtonpost.com/2013-02-20/sports/37202398_1_erick-green-virginia-tech-hokies| accessdate = March 1, 2013}} His lack of production, he later admitted, "turned [him] into a gym rat" and motivated him to work harder than everyone else to improve his game. Each progressive season he increased his scoring, rebounding and assist averages. By his senior season in 2012–13, and while leading NCAA Division I in scoring for most of the year, the media was discussing Green as a [[dark horse]] candidate for [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic Coast Conference Player of the Year]].{{cite web| last =Teel| first =David|title =Is nation's top scorer, Virginia Tech's Erick Green, the ACC's player of the year?| publisher =''[[Daily Press]]''| date =February 5, 2013| url =http://www.dailypress.com/sports/teel-blog/dp-teel-time-green-acc-poy,0,3334715.story| accessdate = March 1, 2013}} Despite his production, the Hokies finished the year with a 13–19 overall record, including a 4–14 conference record where they finished in last place.{{cite web| title =Virginia Tech results| publisher = Virginia Tech| date =February 28, 2013| url =http://www.hokiesports.com/mbasketball/schedule/| accessdate = March 1, 2013}} On March 12, 2013, Green was named the ACC Player of the Year.{{cite web| last =Wood| first =Norm|title =Virginia Tech's Erick Green earns ACC's player of the year honors| publisher =''Daily Press''| date =March 12, 2013| url =http://www.dailypress.com/sports/colleges/virginia-tech/dp-spt-tech-erick-green-acc-player-of-year-0313-20130312,0,862133.story| accessdate = March 12, 2013}} He joined [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]]'s [[Len Bias]] (1985–86) as the only two players of the year who competed for teams with losing ACC records.{{cite web|last=Giannotto| first=Mark |title =Virginia Tech’s Erick
